question.prompt:
The figure shown is called a trefoil and is constructed by drawing circular sectors about sides of the congruent equilateral triangles. What is the area of a trefoil whose horizontal base has length \(2?\)

[Figure 1](figures/2005_AMC_10A_Q12_question_fig1.svg)

solutions.explanation:
To calculate an area using circular sectors, we need their radii and central angles: a sector with radius \(r>0\) and angle \(n^\circ\) has area \(n\pi r^2/360\). The displayed figure shows three two-arc lobes and a horizontal measurement of \(2\), but the equilateral triangles mentioned in the statement are absent. Their arrangement and their relationship to the arcs are unspecified.

Here are two hypothetical constructions illustrating why that information matters. Neither is asserted to be the missing construction. Suppose the three chords joining the common junction to the outer tips have equal length \(c=2/\sqrt3\), with successive chords separated by \(120^\circ\) and the upper chord vertical. The two lower tips are then horizontally \(2\) units apart. Indeed, bisecting the triangle between those chords gives right triangles with hypotenuse \(c\), short leg \(c/2\), and horizontal leg
\[
\sqrt{c^2-(c/2)^2}=\frac{\sqrt3 c}{2}=1.
\]
The short-leg relation follows by halving an equilateral triangle.

First, suppose each lobe consists of two equal circular segments whose arcs subtend \(60^\circ\) at their centers. Each radius is then \(c\). The triangle between the two radii is equilateral, with height \(\sqrt3 c/2\), so its area is \(\sqrt3 c^2/4\). Each circular segment is its sector minus this triangle. The three lobes have total area
\[
T_{60}=6\left(\frac{\pi c^2}{6}-\frac{\sqrt3 c^2}{4}\right)
=\frac{4\pi}{3}-2\sqrt3.
\]

Instead, suppose each arc subtends \(120^\circ\). If its radius is \(r\), splitting the triangle between its radii into two right triangles gives \(c=\sqrt3 r\), hence \(r=2/3\). That triangle has base \(c\) and height \(r/2\), so its area is \(cr/4=\sqrt3 r^2/4\). Now the total area is
\[
T_{120}=6\left(\frac{\pi r^2}{3}-\frac{\sqrt3 r^2}{4}\right)
=\frac{8\pi}{9}-\frac{2\sqrt3}{3}.
\]
In either construction the three lenses have disjoint interiors, so adding their areas counts each part once. Both have the same horizontal tip separation, but their areas differ:
\[
T_{120}-T_{60}=\frac{4(3\sqrt3-\pi)}9>0,
\]
since \(\pi<4<3\sqrt3\).

Thus even a specified symmetric chord arrangement would still require an arc prescription. The omitted equilateral-triangle construction is needed to select the intended area. No numerical choice follows from this display; choice B, \(2\pi/3\), is retained only as the historical key.
solutions.title: Checking what the construction determines
